Advancements in bottom-up synthesis routes for monolayer graphene: a review.
desc: [Royal Society open science] The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.

title: Digital dietitians? Assessing ChatGPT's role in transforming nutrition care and dietetic practice: A systematic review.
desc: [Nutrition and health] BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly being integrated into nutrition care and dietary counseling. Evaluating their usefulness, accuracy, and limitations is essential before widespread clinical adoption.AimTo systematically review the evidence on the performance of ChatGPT and related AI tools in nutrition and dietetics, including comparisons with other AI models and human experts.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and included studies published until February 2025. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar using keywords related to ChatGPT, AI, nutrition, and diet. Of 5504 retrieved records, 31 studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were synthesized under three domains: ChatGPT's performance in nutritional guidance, comparisons with other AI tools, and comparisons with human experts.SummaryMost included studies were cross-sectional and published in 2024, with ChatGPT-3.5 and 4.0 being the most evaluated models. ChatGPT showed high-accuracy in clinical guideline adherence for conditions such as cardiovascular disease and diabetes, moderate performance in dietetics examination simulations, and variable accuracy in disease-specific diet planning. It performed well in nutrition education, dietary recall, and food recognition, but demonstrated limitations in micronutrient estimation, renal nutrition safety, and reproducibility. Compared with other AI tools, ChatGPT showed stronger clinical reasoning but lower performance in specialized food-classification tasks. Compared with human experts, it matched performance in general nutrition knowledge but lacked cultural competence and emotional intelligence. AI tools may complement nutrition care, but human dietitians remain essential for personalized care.

title: Artificial intelligence and small-business competitiveness in an emerging economy.
desc: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are the driving force of developing economies, yet they remain limited in resources to implement artificial intelligence (AI), and there is little empirical evidence that AI adoption is associated with small business growth in the region, particularly in Central Asia. This research makes two contributions. First, we propose a concise framework that links classes of AI technologies to SME competitiveness features and identifies machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI as low-cost, quick-return priority areas for resource-constrained firms. Second, using 16 years of data (2010-2025) for the Bukhara region of Uzbekistan, we estimate ARIMA models for each indicator and forecast eight small business indicators to 2030. Small business output is projected to grow at a steady rate of approximately 16% by 2030, with digital adoption and preferential credit support emerging as indicators associated with long-run growth. Forecast accuracy is high for the human-capital indicator and acceptable for output. The evidence is associational rather than causal: the framework and the forecasts converge on a single, cautiously formulated proposition-the adoption of low-cost AI is measurably associated with the sustainable competitiveness of SMEs, providing a practical, evidence-based starting point for regional AI policy in developing countries.

title: A robust lightweight deep learning network with deformable convolutions for efficient segmentation of optical coherence tomography images.
desc: [Frontiers in digital health] Manual segmentation and evaluation of optical coherence tomography (OCT) images are difficult and rely on specialist training, which limits the output in a busy clinic. While automatic segmentation can ease this burden, the deep models that currently lead the field tend to be too heavy for routine deployment on standard clinical hardware. A further obstacle is the unusual geometry of OCT data: instead of compact objects on a background, the structures of interest form long, undulating tissue strata that extend horizontally across the whole frame, and this layout is poorly matched to convolutional kernels designed for ordinary photographs. We address both issues with LiDeOCTNet, a compact segmentation backbone tailored to the layered nature of OCT. Within a reduced UNet, we introduce learnable sampling offsets so that each kernel can reshape itself locally and trace the curved, irregular interfaces between tissues. To assess the design, we evaluate the network on three OCT collections covering retinal as well as endoscopic acquisitions. Across all three, LiDeOCTNet surpasses a parameter-matched UNet baseline and approaches the accuracy of much heavier benchmarks such as TransUNet, despite using about 750× fewer parameters and running roughly 7.4× faster at inference. Together these properties point to LiDeOCTNet as a practical option for real-time OCT analysis pipelines, including embedded and resource-limited devices.

title: Prioritizing Peptides for Targeted Mass Spectrometry Experiments Using Deep Learning.
desc: [Journal of proteome research] One critical step in any targeted mass spectrometry experiment is selecting, from each protein of interest, a small number of peptides that respond well in the mass spectrometer and can serve as reliable proxies for protein quantification. Existing methods select target peptides either by relying on prior empirical measurements, limiting their applicability to previously observed peptides, or using machine learning to predict peptide behavior from sequence alone. However, current machine learning tools suffer from various limitations, including using detectability as an indirect proxy for intensity, relying on small training sets, or ignoring the precursor charge state. In this study, we introduce Bromo, a transformer-based deep learning model that ranks peptide precursors from a given protein by their relative response, taking charge state into account. Trained on millions of annotated peptide pairs derived from large-scale, publicly available data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry data, Bromo consistently outperforms existing sequence-based methods across diverse, independent data sets. Furthermore, we show that fine-tuning Bromo on experiment-specific data can account for differences in sample preparation, sample matrix, and instrument platform, all of which influence which peptides serve as optimal targets. This adaptability makes Bromo a practical tool for selecting target peptides for selected reaction monitoring and parallel reaction monitoring assay development across a wide range of experimental conditions.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided De Novo Design of High-Affinity Protein Binders Against Shiga Toxin 2.
source: PubMed · Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
desc: [Journal of agricultural and food chemistry] Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) is a major food-borne pathogen with limited treatment options. Targeting Shiga toxin (Stx) represents a promising therapeutic strategy. Using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted de novo protein design combined with bacterial surface display screening, pull-down assays, and biolayer interferometry, we identified protein binders against the Stx2a B subunit (Stx2aB), among which Binder506 exhibited high affinity. Structural modeling predicted a three-α-helix fold, consistent with circular dichroism analysis, while differential scanning fluorimetry revealed high thermostability. Importantly, Binder506 demonstrated potent Stx2a-neutralizing activity with minimal intrinsic cytotoxicity in Vero cells. Size-exclusion chromatography and coimmunoprecipitation showed that Binder506 did not disrupt Stx2a holotoxin integrity. Instead, cellular binding and internalization assays demonstrated that Binder506 inhibited Stx2a attachment to and uptake by Vero cells. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of AI-assisted de novo protein design for generating effective Stx-neutralizing proteins and establish a promising framework for the development of novel therapeutics.

title: Lightweight open-source reasoning large language model for evidence synthesis screening.
desc: [JAMIA open] To evaluate performance and efficiency of a lightweight open-source reasoning large language model (LLM) against an expert-derived reference standard for screening scientific publication databases. Two expert reviewers screened subsets of database records across 3 stages: (1) base eligibility (n = 200), (2) obesity focus (n = 200), and (3) women of reproductive age focus (n = 150). The LLM (gpt-oss-20b) screened all records (n = 20 118). Performance (F1-score and sensitivity [recall]) and efficiency (average screening rate) were assessed. Interreader agreement was near-perfect ( κ : 0.99-1.00; all P < .001). LLM performance was high: F1-score, 0.83-0.94; sensitivity, 90%-95%; specificity, 86%-99%; accuracy, 89%-94%; precision, 77%-99%; and negative predictive value (NPV), 89%-96%. LLM screening was faster than reviewers (19.4 vs ∼1.0 records/min). The LLM achieved high performance and efficiency relative to an expert-derived reference standard for screening. The use of lightweight open-source reasoning LLMs shows promise to support screening in evidence synthesis workflows.

title: Going viral - Virus-targeting nanobodies for research, diagnostics and therapy.
desc: [FEBS letters] The increasing prevalence of viral diseases represents a major threat to global human health, highlighting the urgent need for advanced tools to study viral infections, improve diagnostics, and develop effective antiviral therapies. Antibodies are central to the immune response against viruses and are widely used in research and diagnostics; however, their structural complexity and manufacturing process limit their areas of applications. Single-domain antibodies-better known as nanobodies-derived from heavy chain-only antibodies found in camelids have emerged as a promising alternative. Their unique characteristics-including small size, high stability, the capacity to access cryptic epitopes, and functionality within intracellular environments-make them particularly valuable for viral research. This review highlights recent developments of nanobodies for viral research, diagnostics, and therapeutic applications; discusses their key advantages and limitations; and briefly outlines the emerging role of artificial intelligence-based technologies in facilitating their development to address the expanding burden of viral diseases.

title: Risk stratification in early non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy: the interplay of genetics and cardiac imaging.
desc: [Frontiers in cardiovascular medicine] Preventing sudden cardiac death (SCD) in early non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains a major clinical challenge. Traditional risk stratification centred on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) poorly captures arrhythmic risk, particularly in early dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). Increasing recognition of fibrosis-based and genotype-specific arrhythmogenic substrates has prompted a shift towards multimodal risk assessment strategies integrating imaging, electrocardiographic, and genetic data. This review examines contemporary approaches to risk stratification in early NICM, with particular emphasis on the role of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). The expanding role of genotype-specific phenotyping is also explored, including high-risk arrhythmogenic variants and the integration of genotype with imaging phenotype as a promising route to improved prediction. Collectively, these advances support a transition from population-based LVEF thresholds towards more personalised and biologically informed strategies for prevention of SCD in early NICM.

title: A two-layer model of technology lay beliefs and their societal and political consequences: The case of AI.
desc: [Current opinion in psychology] Modern technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to economic and societal prosperity. Yet, independent of their actual effects, consumers, workers, and the public often hold negative beliefs about these technologies, which can contribute to aversion to AI and technological change more broadly. This article examines technology lay beliefs, with AI as the focal case, and proposes an interconnected two-layer model to explain their societal impact. Layer 1 captures general psychological predispositions to technological change that provide a baseline for why technology lay beliefs often emphasize potential losses. Layer 2 captures specific contextual interpretations of AI that amplify or attenuate this baseline. We use this model to organize existing research and discuss the societal and political consequences of technology lay beliefs in the age of AI.

title: Microfluidic intestinal-chips as next-generation modeling strategies: Multifaceted emerging applications in food research, functional foods and personalized nutrition.
source: PubMed · Current research in food science
desc: [Current research in food science] Food digestion and absorption are essential functions of the human gut and the cornerstone of food research. This article has reviewed the core modeling strategies of intestinal-chips, and their application in the field of food science research, including precise evaluation of nutritional efficacy, food safety risk prediction, innovative development of functional foods and construction of personalized nutritional intervention strategies. Although microfluidic intestinal-chips have addressed some limitations inherent to traditional models, they still face technical challenges in fully replicating the intestinal microenvironment, as well as neural innervation, vascular perfusion and systemic immune responses. Currently, intestinal-chips are accelerating their integration with advanced technologies such as biomaterials, stem cell science, gene editing, 3-D bioprinting and artificial intelligence, to continuously enhance the physiological fidelity, support the optimization of food processing techniques and accelerate the development of new functional foods. These advancements of intestinal-chips won't only substantially promote the industrialization of next-generation food innovations such as cell-cultured meat and synthetic biology foods, but also drive nutritional science research from group recommendations to individualized decision-making. This technology thus provides an indispensable in vitro experimental platform and transformation acceleration engine for achieving "precision nutrition targeting the gut".

title: Deep Learning-Enhanced All-Nanofiber Sensors for Pressure-Temperature Sensing and Stimulus Discrimination.
desc: [Nano letters] Flexible sensors for elderly-assistive robots typically chase high sensitivity, while comfort and multisensory capabilities are largely ignored. Here, we break this pattern with a deep-learning decoupled sensor based on tunable all-nanofiber membranes. Unlike conventional sensors that rely on multiple complex signals, our device uses a single sensing mode and decouples the pressure-temperature signal. The all-nanofiber sensors not only offer excellent pressure-temperature sensing performances but also demonstrate outstanding elderly-friendliness, including biocompatibility, breathability, and degradability. A deep learning algorithm decouples the mixed signals, enabling accurate recognition of liquid temperature and volume in a cup, as well as classification of 15 daily objects during robotic grasping with 97.78% accuracy. This work provides a simple, ecofriendly, and high-performance sensing solution for elderly-assistive robotics and smart home systems.

title: Pharmacological Activities, Biosynthetic Strategies, and Future Prospects: A Comprehensive Review of Baicalein.
source: PubMed · Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
desc: [Journal of agricultural and food chemistry] Baicalein, a 4'-deoxyflavone from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, possesses diverse pharmacological activities including antimicrobial, antifibrotic, antiviral, antitumor, and antioxidant effects. Its effective antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties position it as a promising functional food ingredient and nutraceutical candidate. Traditional production via plant extraction is limited by long growth cycles and low yields, while chemical synthesis uses toxic reagents and harsh conditions. Microbial biosynthesis offers a sustainable alternative. To date, baicalein titers of 367.8 mg/L in Escherichia coli and 401.9 mg/L in Pichia pastoris have been achieved through pathway optimization. However, a systematic review integrating its bioactivities and biosynthesis is still lacking. This review summarizes baicalein's sources, structure, pharmacological activities, and applications, with a focus on heterologous biosynthesis and pathway optimization. Future prospects are also proposed to promote its further biomedical applications and efficient production.

title: Fine-tuning improves deep learning-based digital phenotyping of lettuce genetic resources.
desc: [Frontiers in plant science] Morphological characterization of agricultural genetic resources relies largely on visual assessment by experts, and applying the same criteria repeatedly to large collections is labor-intensive. Image-based deep learning can support this process, but systematic evidence on training strategies suited to genebank trait data remains limited. This study targeted six morphological traits of lettuce genetic resources characterized according to the test guidelines of the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV). Using genebank images accumulated from 2012 to 2025, six convolutional neural networks were trained with three training strategies under identical conditions, and their performance was compared. Fine-tuning achieved the highest mean macro F1-score in 35 of the 36 backbone-trait combinations and significantly outperformed training from scratch and feature extraction, whereas no single backbone was superior across all traits. Misclassifications were concentrated in morphologically adjacent classes rather than randomly distributed, and for the ordinal traits, errors spanning two or more class levels were rare. These patterns suggest that the remaining classification difficulty was associated in part with the morphological continuity between neighboring classes. The attainable performance also differed among traits, distinguishing traits for which the training strategy alone achieved relatively high performance from those for which it did not. These results provide empirical evidence for selecting training strategies and for determining the role of model-assisted characterization on a trait-by-trait basis in genebanks.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Electrochemiluminescence Identification of Latent Fingerprints.
desc: [Analytical chemistry] Latent fingerprints (LFPs) are critical evidence in forensic science, yet their identification usually requires specialized visualization methods that are strongly influenced by the properties of the substrates on which they are deposited. Achieving noninvasive and highly reproducible visualization of LFPs remains a significant challenge. Here, we report the visualization of LFPs on graphite paper (GP) using highly surface-sensitive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) imaging. The imaging mechanism relies on the localized electrochemical inertness of lipid residues on fingerprint ridges, which spatially confines ECL emission to the furrows (uncovered regions), thereby generating a high-contrast negative image with dark ridges against a bright background. In addition, owing to its excellent flexibility and strong lipid-binding capability, GP can serve as both a conductive imaging substrate and a transfer medium for lifting LFP residues from a wide variety of objects, followed by direct ECL visualization without additional treatment, greatly expanding the applicability of this method for personal identification. By further integrating artificial intelligence, we developed an ECL fingerprint identification system that includes database construction, model training, and fingerprint matching, ultimately enabling highly accurate identification of LFPs transferred from 15 types of contact surfaces with matching confidence values greater than 0.94.

title: SMILES-Based Deep Learning Enables Discovery of Chemically Modified Ultrashort Antimicrobial Peptides.
desc: [Journal of medicinal chemistry] Sequence-based models for antimicrobial peptides are limited in representing chemically modified peptides, restricting computational discovery to canonical amino acids. Here, we developed SMAMP, a SMILES-based graph deep learning framework that encodes peptides as molecular graphs and captures noncanonical residues and chemical modifications. SMAMP accurately predicted Escherichia coli MIC (MSE = 0.558, R2 = 0.542, PCC = 0.741), outperforming another SMILES-based baseline. Guided by SMAMP, we designed 19 ultrashort peptides incorporating terminal modifications or noncanonical amino acids, 13 of which exhibited antibacterial activity. Predicted MICs correlated with experimental measurements (r = 0.764). Lead peptides HP-1 and HP-2 showed potent bactericidal activity, low mammalian cytotoxicity, and reduced resistance development compared with conventional antibiotics. Both peptides protected Galleria mellonella from infection and promoted wound healing in mice. Proteomic and mechanistic analyses revealed membrane disruption coupled with oxidative stress. SMAMP provides a chemically informed strategy for discovery and optimization of modified antimicrobial peptides.

title: A hybrid deep learning framework combining CTGAN and transformers for personalized injury mitigation in elite sports.
desc: [Frontiers in physiology] Optimizing training in elite sports while managing injury risk requires models that can learn from heterogeneous and imbalanced athlete records without contaminating evaluation data. This study presents PTI-GANFormer (Personalized Training and Injury Risk Prediction using Generative Adversarial Network-Former), an integrated decision-support framework. Its contribution is not CTGAN or self-attention in isolation; rather, it is the leakage-controlled combination of training-only conditional augmentation, three functionally separated attention pathways, five domain-engineered indicators, and a transparent risk-to-action recommendation layer. After median imputation, plausibility-aware outlier handling, categorical embedding, scaling, and feature engineering, the data were stratified into training and untouched testing partitions. CTGAN was fitted only to the training partition and generated minority-class records until each training class matched the original majority count of 7,894. The hybrid classifier distinguishes No Injury, Minor Injury, and Major Injury, while the recommendation engine converts predicted risk into advisory workload and recovery options that require practitioner review. Across repeated stratified evaluation runs, PTI-GANFormer achieved an accuracy of 0.960 ± 0.004 (95% CI: 0.957-0.963), precision of 0.950 ± 0.006, recall of 0.960 ± 0.005, F1-score of 0.950 ± 0.005, and macro ROC-AUC of 0.981 ± 0.004. These results support predictive risk stratification and decision support; they do not by themselves establish injury prevention or performance enhancement.

title: Accelerated Electrolyte Engineering by Deep Learning: A Quaternary Ammonium Additive Enables Ultra-Stable Zinc Anodes.
desc: [ACS nano] Currently, achieving long-cycling zinc anodes for aqueous zinc-ion energy storage devices remains a challenge owing to uncontrolled dendritic growth and concurrent hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Electrolyte engineering via molecular additives has emerged as an effective strategy for modulating zinc anode interfacial chemistry, but the vast structural space of candidate molecules renders conventional trial-and-error screening inefficient. Here, we present a deep learning (DL) framework for screening high-performance quaternary ammonium cation (QAC) additives for aqueous zinc electrolytes. We developed GATGLP, a graph attention network-based HOMO-LUMO gap (Gap) predictor, to address the data scarcity inherent in ionic molecular systems, which was first pretrained on a curated subset of the QM9 molecular data set and subsequently fine-tuned via transfer learning on a DFT-calculated QAC data set. Through a dual-descriptor screening strategy based on the predicted Gap and the octanol-water partition coefficient (XlogP), a validated library of 378 QAC compounds was ranked, and three candidates were selected for systematic electrochemical validation. Among them, n-octyltrimethylammonium bromide ([N8111]Br) showed a Zn//Zn cycling duration of more than 1800 h at 1 mA cm-2/1 mAh cm-2 and a cycling lifespan of approximately 180 h at 5 mA cm-2/5 mAh cm-2. Across the ZSO-Br, N6111 and N8111 electrolytes, which share the same bromide concentration, three quantities measured by different methods show the same ordering: the relative (002) diffraction proportion, the maximum -Z″ of the impedance arc, and the Zn//Cu sequence length increase from ZSO-Br to N6111 to N8111. The chronoamperometric transient does not follow this ordering, but N8111 is the only electrolyte in which the current magnitude decreases during the step. Taken together, these observations suggest that the selected organic cations may differ in their interfacial accumulation, which could redistribute the Zn deposition flux and contribute to flatter, more continuous deposits. This work combines DL-assisted molecular screening with experimental validation to identify QAC additives for aqueous zinc electrolytes.

title: Ancestral Sequence Reconstruction Synergized with Deep Learning Significantly Enhances the Thermophilicity and Thermostability of the Highly Active Alkaline Protease AprE.
source: PubMed · Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
desc: [Journal of agricultural and food chemistry] Although alkaline proteases have broad industrial applications, their practical use is hindered by insufficient thermostability and limited strategies to elevate optimal catalytic temperature (Topt) while retaining catalytic activity. To enhance Topt and thermostability of Bacillus clausii AprE without sacrificing catalytic performance, this work combined ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) with deep-learning prediction. Ancestral amino acid states were inferred to identify candidate substitution sites for grafting onto the wild-type (WT) backbone, and an ESM-1v-based support vector regression model was built to predict Topt. Systematic screening identified AP291, which exhibited a 4 °C higher Topt and 3.46-fold longer half-life (t1/2) at 60 °C, while maintaining favorable catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) compared with WT AprE. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that AP291 exhibits reduced local structural fluctuations and enhanced conformational stability, clarifying the underlying stability-enhancing mechanism. This work presents a synergistic ASR-deep learning strategy for enzyme engineering, and AP291 is promising for industrial biocatalysis.
